## Functions and Change {#vol-04 .section-title}


## Chapter Map {#chapter-map .section-title}

```{=html}
<div class="wh-book-grid wh-reveal">
  <article class="wh-book-card">
    <span class="wh-book-card__status">Ch 1</span>
    <div class="wh-book-card__title"><a href="./01-exponents-logarithms.html">Exponents and logarithms</a></div>
    <div class="wh-book-card__desc">Managing multiplicative growth. Exponential functions and their inverses — logarithms as the answer to "what power gives me this result?"</div>
  </article>
  <article class="wh-book-card">
    <span class="wh-book-card__status">Ch 2</span>
    <div class="wh-book-card__title"><a href="./02-complex-numbers.html">Complex numbers</a></div>
    <div class="wh-book-card__desc">Expanding the number plane. The imaginary unit as a rotation, Argand diagrams, polar form, and why complex numbers solve problems real numbers cannot.</div>
  </article>
  <article class="wh-book-card">
    <span class="wh-book-card__status">Ch 3</span>
    <div class="wh-book-card__title"><a href="./03-systems-matrices.html">Systems and matrices</a></div>
    <div class="wh-book-card__desc">Handling multiple relationships at once. Matrix notation, row reduction, determinants, and the geometric meaning of a system of linear equations.</div>
  </article>
  <article class="wh-book-card">
    <span class="wh-book-card__status">Ch 4</span>
    <div class="wh-book-card__title"><a href="./04-sequences-series.html">Sequences and series</a></div>
    <div class="wh-book-card__desc">Identifying and summing discrete patterns. Convergence, geometric series, and the surprising fact that infinitely many terms can have a finite sum.</div>
  </article>
  <article class="wh-book-card">
    <span class="wh-book-card__status">Ch 5</span>
    <div class="wh-book-card__title"><a href="./05-partial-fractions.html">Partial fractions</a></div>
    <div class="wh-book-card__desc">Breaking a complicated fraction into simpler pieces. A technique that appears in integration and in Laplace transforms — decomposing to compute.</div>
  </article>
  <article class="wh-book-card">
    <span class="wh-book-card__status">Ch 6</span>
    <div class="wh-book-card__title"><a href="./06-phasors-waveforms.html">Phasors and alternating waveforms</a></div>
    <div class="wh-book-card__desc">A rotating complex number traces a sine wave. Phasors let you do AC circuit analysis with algebra instead of trigonometric identities.</div>
  </article>
</div>
```
